exposure: Quality improvement (QI) initiative (staff training, parent education via Neo-MILK app)
Growth sufficient exclusive breast milk feeding at 14 days postpartum
outcome: Breastfeeding rate at 4 months after birth
Growth sufficient exclusive breast milk feeding at 14 days after birth
cohort: 69 mothers and their moderate and late preterm infants (gestational age 32-36 weeks) participated in the study.
finding: The implementation of a quality improvement initiative was associated with a significant increase in medium-term breastfeeding success (75% vs 48%) in moderate and late preterm infants.
mod_finding: Delivery by cesarean section was associated with lower medium-term breastfeeding success.
